basis: Expanded from the repository's existing World / Plane branches without deleting prior nodes.

nodes.name: Universe
nodes.description: The total physical cosmos considered as the largest empirical frame for astronomy, matter, energy and spacetime.

nodes.name: Cosmos
nodes.description: The ordered whole of existence; a conceptual frame spanning physical cosmology and philosophical accounts of order.

nodes.name: Galaxies
nodes.description: Large gravitationally bound systems of stars, gas, dust, dark matter and associated structures.

nodes.name: Stars
nodes.description: Self-gravitating luminous bodies whose nuclear processes shape cosmic structure and produce many chemical elements.

nodes.name: Solar System
nodes.description: The planetary system organized around the Sun, including planets, moons, asteroids, comets and smaller bodies.

nodes.name: Sun
nodes.description: The star at the center of the Solar System and its dominant source of radiant energy.

nodes.name: Moon
nodes.description: Earth's natural satellite, important to tides, calendars, night illumination and human cultural symbolism.

nodes.name: Planets
nodes.description: Large bodies orbiting the Sun, including Earth and the other recognized planets of the Solar System.

nodes.name: Physics
nodes.description: Study of matter, energy, motion, fields, spacetime and the fundamental interactions of nature.

nodes.name: Chemistry
nodes.description: Study of substances, their composition, properties, reactions and transformations.

nodes.name: Chemical Elements
nodes.description: Fundamental chemical species defined by atomic number and organized in the periodic table.

nodes.name: Energy
nodes.description: A conserved physical quantity associated with the capacity for change, motion, work and interaction.

nodes.name: Earth
nodes.description: The inhabited planet and physical setting for the repository's terrestrial geography, climate and life branches.

nodes.name: Geography
nodes.description: Study and description of places, spatial relationships, landscapes, regions and human-environment systems.

nodes.name: Continents
nodes.description: Major continental landmasses used as a first-order geographic organization of the world.

nodes.name: Oceans
nodes.description: Large interconnected bodies of salt water governing climate, ecosystems, transport, resources and planetary circulation.

nodes.name: Atmosphere
nodes.description: The gaseous envelope surrounding Earth and a major regulator of weather, climate and life.

nodes.name: Climate
nodes.description: Long-term statistical patterns of weather and the interacting physical systems that shape them.

nodes.name: Water
nodes.description: H2O as a planetary substance essential to life, climate, agriculture, industry, ecosystems and human settlement.

nodes.name: Ecosystems
nodes.description: Communities of organisms interacting with one another and with their physical environment.

nodes.name: Plants
nodes.description: Photosynthetic organisms forming foundational components of terrestrial and aquatic food webs and ecosystems.

nodes.name: Agriculture
nodes.description: Cultivation of plants and management of animals, soils, water and landscapes for food, fibre and other products.

nodes.name: Microorganisms
nodes.description: Microscopic organisms and biological agents central to ecosystems, disease, fermentation, nutrient cycles and biotechnology.

nodes.name: Cells
nodes.description: Basic structural and functional units of cellular life.

nodes.name: Genetics
nodes.description: Study of heredity, genes, genomes and the transmission and expression of biological information.

nodes.name: Evolution
nodes.description: Change in inherited characteristics of populations across generations, including natural selection and other evolutionary mechanisms.

nodes.name: Neuroscience
nodes.description: Study of nervous systems, brains, neural circuits and their relationships to behaviour and cognition.

nodes.name: Cognition
nodes.description: Processes involved in perception, memory, learning, reasoning, attention, decision-making and mental representation.

nodes.name: Language
nodes.description: Structured symbolic communication through which people transmit meaning, knowledge, identity and culture.

nodes.name: Culture
nodes.description: Shared meanings, practices, symbols, knowledge, norms and creative expressions transmitted across people and generations.

nodes.name: Education
nodes.description: Formal and informal systems for transmitting knowledge, skills, values and capabilities across generations.

nodes.name: Art
nodes.description: Creative production and interpretation through visual, material, performative and conceptual forms.

nodes.name: Music
nodes.description: Organized sound and musical practice used for expression, coordination, ritual, memory, entertainment and identity.

nodes.name: Families
nodes.description: Kinship and household structures through which care, identity, inheritance and intergenerational relationships are organized.

nodes.name: Communities
nodes.description: Groups connected by place, identity, practice, interest or shared institutions.

nodes.name: Cities
nodes.description: Dense human settlements concentrating people, institutions, infrastructure, production, culture and exchange.

nodes.name: States
nodes.description: Territorial political organizations exercising public authority through institutions, law, taxation, administration and security.

nodes.name: Constitutions
nodes.description: Foundational arrangements defining public authority, institutions, rights and procedures of political order.

nodes.name: Diplomacy
nodes.description: Methods and institutions through which political actors negotiate, represent interests and manage international relationships.

nodes.name: Military
nodes.description: Organized armed forces and associated command, logistics, intelligence, procurement and strategic capabilities.

nodes.name: Justice
nodes.description: Systems and ideas concerning rights, duties, fairness, adjudication, punishment, remedy and legitimate order.

nodes.name: Religion
nodes.description: Traditions and communities concerned with sacred meaning, ritual, revelation, transcendence, ethics and ultimate questions.

nodes.name: Philosophy
nodes.description: Systematic inquiry into reality, knowledge, reason, value, mind, language and the good life.

nodes.name: Science
nodes.description: Organized empirical inquiry using observation, measurement, modelling, testing, criticism and reproducible evidence.

nodes.name: Mathematics
nodes.description: Formal study of quantity, structure, space, change, logic, patterns and abstract relationships.

nodes.name: Medicine
nodes.description: Evidence-based prevention, diagnosis, treatment and management of human disease and injury.

nodes.name: Health
nodes.description: Condition and systems of physical and mental functioning, prevention, care and population health.

nodes.name: Electricity
nodes.description: Electrical phenomena and the generation, transmission, distribution, storage and use of electrical power.

nodes.name: Oil & Gas
nodes.description: Hydrocarbon resources and the extraction, processing, transport, trade and use systems built around them.

nodes.name: Minerals
nodes.description: Geological materials extracted for construction, industry, energy, electronics, manufacturing and strategic supply chains.

nodes.name: Manufacturing
nodes.description: Transformation of materials and components into goods through industrial processes, machinery, labour and technology.

nodes.name: Logistics
nodes.description: Planning and movement of goods, materials, inventories and information through supply chains.

nodes.name: Transport
nodes.description: Systems moving people and goods by road, rail, sea, air and other modes.

nodes.name: Aviation
nodes.description: Aircraft, airports, air navigation, airlines, regulation and the global movement of people and cargo by air.

nodes.name: Telecommunications
nodes.description: Networks and systems carrying voice, data and signals through fibre, radio, satellites and other media.
